The csv file Neuropathic_28.csv contains neuropathic pain diagnosis records in the form of tables of which the row represents different patients and the column represents different diagnostic labels.

Which cause-and-effect relationship is more likely?
A. L lateral arm discomfort causes R C6 radiculopathy
B. R C6 radiculopathy causes L lateral arm discomfort
C. No causal relationship exists

content.text:
The two variables are associated: the correlation is about 0.064, and L lateral arm discomfort appears in 100 of the 4,076 patients with R C6 radiculopathy but in only 101 of the 12,308 without it. So option C (no causal relationship) is unlikely.

The data can't show the direction of the link on its own. Anatomically, radiculopathy is the pathophysiological diagnosis and arm discomfort is the symptom it produces, so radiculopathy causing the symptom (B) is the more plausible direction. The opposite, a symptom causing a nerve-root lesion, makes little sense. I chose B on that reasoning, not on a test of direction in the data.

ANSWER: B
